summary.text: John Whipple is the Democratic candidate for Kentucky House of Representatives District 10, running against incumbent Republican Josh Calloway in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A retired U.S. Army veteran who worked in public education as a teacher and school administrator, he has run for the seat before.

paragraphs.text: John Whipple was born in Corona, California, and served in the United States Army from 1980 to 2003.

He earned an associate degree in technical instruction from the Community College of the Air Force, a bachelor's degree in liberal arts from Excelsior College and a master's degree in education leadership from the University of Cincinnati in 2010, and he also attended the Defense Language Institute.

Whipple worked in public education as a teacher and in school administration, has served as a board member with the Kentucky Education Association and has volunteered with Court Appointed Special Advocates for Children.
In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey, Whipple said he began teaching eighth-grade social studies in Breckinridge County, Kentucky, in 2004 and was president of the Breckinridge County Education Association.
He ran for Kentucky State Senate District 5 in 2020, losing to incumbent Stephen Meredith, and for Kentucky House District 10 in 2022 and 2024, losing each time to Calloway.
In a 2020 survey he described himself as a progressive Independent candidate.
In his 2025 Ballotpedia survey, Whipple named public school funding, protections and collective bargaining rights for Kentucky workers, and respect for all people among his key messages.
